clue.text: Take away 23 ac-or 25?

parts.note: taking the stars off an officer's shoulder lowers rank, and the second option jokes that removing a speck is a de-speck, prefixing the word for a speck with de-

explanation.surface: A puzzling choice between removing one thing or another, phrased like a cross-reference quiz.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 across gives PIPS, the stars marking an army officer's rank; removing them lowers the officer. 25 down is MOTE, and DE- plus that speck spells the answer as a pun.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip an officer of rank insignia is to reduce rank, and the pun splits the word into de- plus a speck.

clue.text: Father clutches child to keep away from dog

indicators.note: clutches means the word for father holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: dad is an informal word for father
to shun is to avoid or keep away from

explanation.surface: A father grabs his child to keep it away from a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clutches' puts CH and SHUN inside DAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The badger hound is a long-bodied, short-legged German breed.

clue.text: A drink for Clementine's dad Albert

parts.note: in the song 'Oh My Darling, Clementine' her father was a miner, forty-niner
Al is the short form of Albert

explanation.surface: Ordering a round for a girl's father named Albert.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a mineral is a fizzy soft drink, short for mineral water.
explanation.definitionFit: Mineral is an old British word for a carbonated soft drink such as lemonade.

clue.text: General Tom's men pressed for an answer

definitions.note: names a torture device that squeezes fingers to force a confession

parts.note: General Tom Thumb was the stage name of a tiny performer exhibited by P. T. Barnum
a crew is a group of men working together

explanation.surface: A small general's soldiers are interrogated.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes what the device did: squeezed a prisoner's digits to force a confession.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument of torture crushed a victim's digits until they confessed.

clue.text: Henry said Daniel is a spiteful old woman

indicators.note: said signals that the pet name for Henry is taken by its pronunciation, not its usual spelling

parts.note: Harry is the familiar form of the name Henry

explanation.surface: Someone reports what Henry said about Daniel, who is called nasty names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' makes HARRY into its sound-alike HARRI, then DAN follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrew or scold: an old woman known for bad temper and spite.

clue.text: It's played after the deuce

parts.note: in tennis, the point won after the score reaches forty-all gives this lead

explanation.surface: Something played following a two in cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deuce' suggests a playing card, the two; in tennis it is forty-all, and the next point won gives the server or receiver this.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis this is the score called when a player wins the point after deuce.

clue.text: Petroleum's constituent part

indicators.note: constituent means forming part of something, so the answer is found within the word Petroleum

explanation.surface: Asks what component goes into making oil.
explanation.definitionFit: A role is the part played by an actor or a person.

clue.text: Type of rhomb

parts.note: a rhomb is a rhombus, an equal-sided slanted quadrilateral, the shape on playing cards' red suit

explanation.surface: A geometric query about a slanted shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The playing card suit symbol and the lozenge shape are both rhombuses.

clue.text: She looks after kids

parts.note: reads as a childminder, but kids are also young goats, whose mother is a female goat

explanation.surface: A childminder at work.
explanation.walkthrough: Both a children's nurse and a she-goat, the mother of kids, carry the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's nurse cares for youngsters, and a female goat cares for kids.

clue.text: Do you know John, after whom Bobby was named?

definitions.meaning: the hunting song 'D'ye ken John ...' asks whether you know the Cumbrian huntsman
British policemen are called bobbies after Sir Robert ..., who founded the Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you know the John that a child named Bobby was named after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'D'ye ken John Peel' is an old English hunting song; a bobby is a British police officer, named after Robert Peel.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's huntsman surname and the policing founder's surname are the same.

clue.text: About to make certain of blame

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about, as in dates
to ensure is to make certain

explanation.surface: A person is about to make sure who is at fault.
explanation.definitionFit: To censure someone is to criticise or condemn them formally, a verb of reproach.

clue.text: Crook gets in at the back of the house

indicators.note: at the back of places one piece behind another, so the short word follows the dwelling

parts.note: a villa is a house, especially a large suburban or country one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A burglar sneaks into a home through the rear entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A crook is a criminal, a wrongdoer or rogue.

clue.text: Prize-fighter Tom wearing arm support is writing badly

indicators.note: wearing puts the boxer inside the arm support, as if he has it on

parts.note: a sling supports an injured arm
Tom Cribb was a famous English bare-knuckle boxing champion of the early 1800s

explanation.surface: A boxer with his arm in a sling has terrible handwriting.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Cribb (1781-1848) was an English bare-knuckle champion; CRIBB goes inside SLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrawling hastily or carelessly with a pen is scrawl-like penmanship.

clue.text: Capture Barbary's last ape

parts.note: to cop is slang for to catch or capture

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word Barbary's

explanation.surface: An instruction to catch the last remaining Barbary ape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ape' looks like the animal from the surface, but it is the verb: to imitate. Barbary apes live on the Rock of Gibraltar.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to mimic or imitate them, which is to reproduce them.

clue.text: Could this make chairman so drunk ?

definitions.text: Could this make chairman so drunk

indicators.note: drunk means intoxicated, so the letters of the two words reel into a new order

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a cherry liqueur could get the chairman tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges CHAIRMAN SO, and the whole clue describes the liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet cherry liqueur strong enough to intoxicate a chairman.

clue.text: Ill-fated.? Not Jim !

parts.note: un- is a prefix meaning not
Lucky Jim is the 1954 comic novel by Kingsley Amis, so Jim suggests his nickname

explanation.surface: Someone protests that their fate was poor, unlike a certain Jim.
explanation.walkthrough: Lucky Jim is a famous Kingsley Amis novel; its hero's epithet follows UN.
explanation.definitionFit: Doomed or hapless people are those with bad fortune.

clue.text: When Caesar's word " might have stood against the world "

definitions.text: When Caesar's word " might have stood against the world "

parts.words: When Caesar's word " might have stood against the world "
parts.note: quotes Mark Antony in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar: 'But ___ the word of Caesar might have stood against the world'

explanation.surface: A quiz question on when Caesar's word carried weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Antony's funeral speech in Julius Caesar laments that only a day before, Caesar's word was all-powerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Antony's line says that only the day before, Caesar's command was supreme.

clue.text: An orchestra on leave

parts.note: an gives the indefinite article A
a band is a group of musicians, a small orchestra
taken as written

explanation.surface: A whole orchestra is away on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something behind for good is to desert or forsake it.

clue.text: Let this vain youth repair castle's ruins

indicators.note: repair means put back together, so the letters of the fodder are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Telling a conceited young man to fix a ruined castle.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: LET plus the answer, rearranged ('repair'), makes CASTLES RUINS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the beautiful youth fell in love with his own reflection.

clue.text: The devil wrote books

definitions.meaning: as in 'what the ...?', an old euphemism for the devil
Charles ... was the Victorian novelist who wrote Oliver Twist and David Copperfield

explanation.surface: Satan himself turns author.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the novelist Charles is also a mild oath standing in for Satan.

clue.text: First-class letter

explanation.surface: Posting a letter by the faster mail service.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means excellent as an adjective and an upper-case character as a noun.

clue.text: Receding hair added to our charm

indicators.note: receding means going back, so the word for hair is read from right to left

parts.note: a mane is a long head of hair
taken as written

explanation.surface: A balding man finds his thinning hair only adds to his appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receding' turns MANE into ENAM; 'added to' puts OUR after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to make them fond of you, to captivate them.

clue.text: Forced to be grateful

definitions.meaning: compelled or required to do something
thankful, as in 'I'm much ___ to you'

explanation.surface: Someone made to be thankful.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both compelled and indebted for a favour.

clue.text: Master Pirrip's way of telling the time

definitions.meaning: Philip Pirrip, called Pip, is the boy hero of Dickens's Great Expectations, so this is his possessive
the BBC radio time signal is a series of short beeps called the ...

explanation.surface: A young gentleman's method for reading a clock.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greenwich Time Signal on BBC radio is six short beeps known in Britain as the pips.
explanation.definitionFit: Pip's (the Great Expectations boy's) and the radio time signal beeps share one spelling.

clue.text: Sound fruit's sound

indicators.note: the second sound tells us the fruit word is to be taken as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: a plum is a fruit

explanation.surface: Is a piece of fruit healthy?
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Sound' is the verb to measure depth, not 'healthy'.
explanation.definitionFit: To plumb is to measure depth with a weighted line, as sailors sound the sea.

clue.text: Strange vice, miller producing thin pasta

indicators.note: strange signals the letters of the two words are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: A miller with an odd vice turns his flour into noodles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges VICE MILLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for little worms, these are very slender strands of spaghetti-like noodle.

clue.text: With car test examiner's first to discover a minor fault

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British cars, from the Ministry of Transport

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word examiner's

explanation.surface: A vehicle inspector spots a small defect.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's yearly compulsory vehicle safety check.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblically, a speck in another's eye, so a trivial flaw.

clue.text: No 29 for her

definitions.meaning: 29 across is a centre-of-target hit, so not one is a failure to hit
the title for an unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A cross-reference that seems to say a woman got number 29.
explanation.definitionFit: A failed shot, and the title for a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Discomposed, I turned green

indicators.note: discomposed means unsettled, so the letters of the two words are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone upset goes pale and queasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' wants to be the colour of nausea; it means inexperienced. 'Discomposed' rearranges I TURNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or new, never yet tested in practice.

clue.text: Shooting pains make Gemini hold their heads

indicators.note: hold means the word for the zodiac pair contains the other letters

parts.note: Gemini, the zodiac sign, is the Twins
their refers back to Gemini, and its opening pair of letters is G and E

explanation.surface: Twins clutching their heads in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' puts GE, the first two letters of 'Gemini', inside TWINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden sharp stabs of discomfort are brief darting aches.

clue.text: A good shot, the glass boss

definitions.meaning: a hit in the centre of a target is the best shot
... glass is old window glass with a thick round knob, or boss, at its centre

explanation.surface: A marksman's praise for a hit, or a boss with a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: The centre of a dartboard or target, and the central lump left in hand-blown crown glass.

clue.text: Tribesmen riot in Rhodes

indicators.note: a riot is wild disorder, so the letters of the island name are thrown into confusion

explanation.surface: Unrest breaks out among tribal people on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riot' rearranges RHODES.
explanation.definitionFit: Hordes are large nomadic bands, originally of Tartar or Mongol tribes.
